        12                  THE SECRETARY:    By Senator

        13       Martins, legislative resolution celebrating

        14       the opening of an exhibit at The Holocaust

        15       Memorial and Tolerance Center of Nassau County

        16       recognizing the life and heroic actions of

        17       Aristides de Sousa Mendes.

        18                  ACTING PRESIDENT FLANAGAN:

        19       Senator Martins on the resolution.

        20                  SENATOR MARTINS:    Thank you,

        21       Mr. President.

        22                  I rise and ask my colleagues to

        23       join me in recognizing not only The Holocaust

        24       Memorial and Tolerance Center of Nassau

        25       County, which is the preeminent center in



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                                         643



         1       Nassau County for teachings on the Holocaust

         2       and on tolerance, but also the life of a very

         3       special individual, Aristides de Sousa Mendes,

         4       who was a consul general for Portugal in

         5       Bordeaux, France, during World War II.

         6                  During six days in June of 1940,

         7       against the orders of his government,

         8       Aristides de Sousa Mendes issued over 30,000

         9       visas to individuals fleeing the Nazi regime.

        10       As they tried to leave France, he gave them

        11       safe passage.  Included among those 30,000 are

        12       12,000 Jews who were saved during World War

        13       II, the consequences of which are readily

        14       apparent.  There are hundreds of thousands of

        15       people alive today in the world as a result of

        16       this one individual's actions.

        17                  And there are times like these that

        18       we have an opportunity as a body to recognize

        19       those people who have made a difference in

        20       this world against the interests of their own

        21       self-interest, against the orders of their own

        22       government, taking a stand for that which is

        23       right.  And Aristides de Sousa Mendes was just

        24       such a person.

        25                  Unfortunately, he died in 1954,



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                                         644



         1       stripped of all diplomatic credentials,

         2       stripped of his right to practice in his

         3       country, but was recognized in 1966 by Israel

         4       at Yad Vashem as one of the Righteous Among

         5       the Nations.

         6                  The Holocaust and Tolerance Center

         7       in Nassau County opened an exhibit yesterday

         8       recognizing the life of Aristides de Sousa

         9       Mendes, a person of singular integrity and

        10       courage who unquestionably altered world

        11       history and certainly altered the lives of so

        12       many hundreds of thousands of individuals.

        13                  I think it is incumbent upon us,

        14       when we do have an example of extraordinary

        15       courage and character, that we recognize such

        16       an individual.  And I would ask my colleagues

        17       to join with me in recognizing Aristides de

        18       Sousa Mendes for his great contribution to

        19       society as well as his great example to

        20       today's generation and future generations of

        21       courage and character under extraordinary

        22       circumstances.

        23                  Thank you, Mr. President.
